stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: US arrests tech CEO accused of smuggling $300M in Nvidia chips into China
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A US tech CEO has been arrested for allegedly smuggling $300 million worth of Nvidia chips into China.
The incident highlights ongoing and persistent challenges related to technology export controls and illicit trade.
The case underscores the geopolitical tensions surrounding advanced semiconductor technology between the US and China.

stories.title: Run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (125B) on consumer hardware (RTX 4090) at 100T/s
stories.author: snehesht
bullet_points: Demonstrates the feasibility of running a massive LLM (Qwen 3.8 Flash, 125B parameters) on high-end consumer GPUs.
Achieves a high inference speed of 100T/s on an RTX 4090, indicating significant performance gains.
Suggests a major shift towards democratizing large-scale AI model deployment outside of specialized data centers.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and performance tracking for Meta's latest instruction-tuned model.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags like 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking around a major LLM release.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for running complex, multi-step tasks and tool-calling locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and lower memory usage for models.
The updated engine also contributes to higher quality output from the language models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Apple changes full-disk access permissions to curb abuse from AI agents
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Apple is modifying full-disk access permissions to mitigate misuse by AI agents.
The change addresses concerns regarding unauthorized access to user data by third-party AI applications.
The article highlights a disagreement between Meta and the FDA regarding the sufficiency of current regulations for AI message reading.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Introduces GALA, a distillation method to solve the real-time animation bottleneck in 3D Gaussian avatars.
The core finding is that complex avatar animations can be approximated by a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes.
GALA replaces expensive per-frame neural decoding with a lightweight, shallow coefficient predictor for faster rendering.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new fine-grained benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often overlook the practical necessity of accurate command-line interface (CLI) syntax in cybersecurity workflows.
Features runtime-free verifiable rewards, suggesting a novel and rigorous method for assessing tool-use proficiency without requiring full execution environments.

stories.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
stories.author: Kaiming He
bullet_points: Introduces VISTA, a new visual harness designed to unlock reasoning potential in multimodal AI models.
VISTA provides general-purpose multimodal models with long-horizon vision capabilities in interactive environments.
The system features a lossless visual memory, allowing the model to actively retrieve and process past visual observations.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in real-time animation of 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to approximate complex avatar animations using a linear combination of blendshapes.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a much faster, shallow coefficient predictor for real-time performance.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical gap in LLM capabilities: determining if their mathematical solutions stem from true structural understanding.
The paper introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a novel method to systematically probe and diagnose mathematical reasoning in LLMs.
The findings aim to guide future improvements in LLMs through targeted post-training techniques based on diagnostic insights.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often lack direct measurement of CLI command generation accuracy, a necessity in cybersecurity operations.
Features runtime-free verifiable rewards, suggesting a novel approach to assessing the correctness of generated tool invocations.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new decision models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, or scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services (Claude) with local, open-source LLM infrastructure (Ollama).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
Integration with llama.cpp broadens the range of supported models and hardware capabilities.
The update augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: An AI couldn’t beat humans at StarCraft, so it decided to cheat
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: A competitive AI vs. human bot tournament (StarSkirmish) is underway using StarCraft.
Advanced models like GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 performed well but were outperformed by a top human-made bot, Stardust.
The story touches on the current limitations of AI in complex, strategic tasks like real-time strategy gaming.

stories.title: Capcom is preparing for a ‘future where we create games together with AI’
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Capcom is actively exploring the integration of AI into game development processes.
A programmer presented on the future evolution of the RE Engine, suggesting ongoing technical development.
The news indicates a shift towards collaborative game creation involving AI, moving beyond just in-game horror themes.

stories.title: Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Amazon's $1B initiative to address data center concerns is facing criticism.
The company received praise for ending Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs).
However, Amazon is being criticized for minimizing the environmental impact of its data centers.

stories.title: Lyft settles landmark driver misclassification lawsuit for $272.5M
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: Lyft has settled a major lawsuit concerning the misclassification of its drivers.
The settlement amount reached $272.5 million.
The resolution faces criticism from groups claiming drivers are owed additional compensation.

stories.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces RPG, a framework for autonomous improvement of robot execution systems.
The method allows for skill improvement without requiring updates to the underlying model weights.
RPG uses offline datasets to identify capabilities and generates simulation-based practice tasks using execution feedback.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test a crucial human skill in scientific research.
The benchmark focuses on the ability to identify prior research papers that inspire or advance new scientific projects.
It leverages expert annotation from researchers to create a scalable dataset for studying idea retrieval in scientific literature.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces SILSA, a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation.
Addresses limitations of current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
Uses compact sliding-window slice latents to maintain topology awareness during 3D shape generation.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) are presented as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
CDLMs aim to overcome the statistical dependency limitations found in discrete models when performing parallel decoding.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, which is central to avoiding token independence issues.

stories.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
stories.author: Chongyang Ma
bullet_points: Introduces DMAD (Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation) for faster visual generation.
DMAD reframes distribution matching as a classification problem to learn log-density ratios directly.
It aims to improve upon existing methods that require auxiliary diffusion models, reducing memory and computation costs.

stories.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduces Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR) to address limitations in molecular learning models.
HGR is designed to explicitly encode complex molecular topologies, such as ring systems and recurring motifs, which standard formalisms struggle with.
The framework aims to provide a principled, topology-aware method that is computationally feasible compared to existing high-order representations.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings instead of fixed class labels or text prompts to condition image generation in diffusion transformers.
The core methodology involves training a Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA) model to forecast the subsequent continuous embedding in a sequence.
This approach leverages the inherent sequential nature of image generation (noisy to clean image) to train the predictive model.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces SILSA, a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation.
Addresses limitations of current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
Uses compact sliding-window slice latents to represent shapes while preserving topology.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO introduces a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The optimizer achieves sparsity by using a Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse approach, addressing memory limitations on modern GPUs.
TACO is presented as an alternative to existing methods (like Muon) that either compress state or alter update geometry, aiming to maintain performance comparable to AdamW.

stories.title: Cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control
stories.author: Akshay Balsubramani
bullet_points: The paper presents an exact solution for cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges defined on graphs.
It replaces complex learned control mechanisms (like temporal-difference penalties) with a mathematical technique called a Feynman-Kac tilt.
This simplification allows the cost-augmented bridge to be computed exactly against a tilted reference process.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models mitigate this by denoising a shared continuous state, though the current description notes a limitation in the denoiser's scope.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale LLM fine-tuning.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size.
ZFO uses a first-order optimizer for direction and zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the ability to retrieve inspiring prior research papers.
The benchmark leverages expert knowledge, using researchers to annotate which past works influenced their current projects.
Addresses the challenge of AI systems needing to sense relevant, buried ideas within the massive corpus of scientific literature.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models overcome this by denoising a shared continuous state, allowing for better modeling of token relationships.

stories.title: Every Ablation Is a Dose: Counterweights and the Semblance of Self-Repair
stories.author: Vinay Kumar Sankarapu
bullet_points: The paper investigates the phenomenon of 'self-repair' in language models, where components compensate when others are removed (ablated).
Previous research suggested self-repair is noisy and lacks a single explanatory mechanism.
The authors propose a novel hypothesis: self-repair is rooted in an inherent gain present in the model even before any intervention.

stories.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Xin Dong
bullet_points: Introduces AutoCompact, a method to train coding agents to intelligently manage context in long-horizon software engineering tasks.
Addresses the problem of stale context in complex coding tasks, requiring agents to decide when and how to compact their working state.
The approach integrates context management decisions directly into the agent's policy during training.

stories.title: From Knowledge Access to Source Learning: Developing Source-Specific Competence
stories.author: Haohan Wang
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in current LLM agents where repeated use of the same external knowledge source is treated merely as repeated access.
The core concept introduced is 'source learning,' which aims to allow LLMs to progressively improve their understanding of a specific external source over time.
This work builds upon existing methods for knowledge access and agent memory by focusing on developing reusable, source-specific competence within LLM systems.

stories.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
stories.author: Juan S. Santillana
bullet_points: Keyword-matching benchmarks can produce false positives, incorrectly crediting small language models for tool use they do not actually perform.
The paper proposes a 'cheap diagnostic ladder' to provide stricter and more reliable evaluations of tool-use capabilities in LLMs.
The study demonstrates this issue using a matched-architecture pair of Spanish security language models, highlighting the limitations of lenient metrics.

stories.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: The paper proposes a novel finetuning technique that leverages sampling to improve model capabilities.
It challenges the conventional view that Reinforcement Learning (RL) is superior to Supervised Finetuning (SFT) for generalization.
The research addresses the trade-off between SFT's ability to use off-policy data and RL's generalization strengths.

stories.title: Argo-Bench: Evaluating Data Agents on Enterprise-Scale Workflows
stories.author: Joseph J Ma
bullet_points: Argo-Bench addresses the limitations of existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, which only test query generation.
The framework evaluates 'Data Agents' on complex, enterprise-scale workflows requiring reasoning across multiple tables and statistical analysis.
It uses public datasets to simulate real-world enterprise scenarios due to the sensitivity of actual corporate data.

stories.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
stories.author: Spyros Gidaris
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Where-OPD,' a method applying on-policy self-distillation to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
This technique uses a student model supervised by a privileged, frozen version of itself, which is a novel application of self-distillation to multimodal contexts.
It aims to overcome limitations in current MLLM approaches that rely on localized visual cues (like image crops) for fine-grained perception.

stories.title: Show HN: AI search for every photo and every frame of video on macOS
stories.author: allenleee
bullet_points: A new 'Show HN' project introduces AI search capabilities for photos and video frames on macOS.
The tool leverages AI/ML to enable granular searching within visual media libraries.
This represents a practical application of AI in enhancing local operating system functionality.

stories.title: I got targeted: Trying to get your credentials via a git post-checkout hook
stories.author: frankwiles.com by frankwiles
bullet_points: The article discusses a security vulnerability related to Git post-checkout hooks.
The attack vector involves attempting to steal user credentials via these hooks.
This highlights a specific, practical security risk within developer workflows.

stories.title: Your CDN can overrule robots.txt: finding the layer that refuses AI crawlers
stories.author: mahirhir
bullet_points: The article investigates a vulnerability where Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) might override standard robots.txt directives.
It specifically focuses on how this mechanism affects AI crawlers, such as GPTBot.
The initial finding involved Japanese tourism sites exhibiting contradictory behavior between their robots.txt and server configuration.
